title: Paged KV granularity harmonizer and decode-wave fairness
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Goal: Reduce decode latency tail and KV thrashing for mixed small/large requests by introducing a lightweight coordinator that harmonizes KV allocation granularity with decode-wave scheduling. This ticket implements the "harmonizer": a runtime component that decides when to coalesce adjacent small KV fragments into temporary "micro-views" and when to favor fine-grained residency, plus a decode-wave fairness policy that staggers prefill and decode starts to avoid bursty memory pressure and kernel hot-path contention.
background: We observe two failure modes in production for paged attention workloads: (1) many concurrent short traces (e.g., chat turns, search rerank) allocate many small KV fragments that cause high fragmentation and frequent eviction cycles; (2) decode waves (batches that enter the decoder) are synchronized across tenants/streams and create simultaneous prefill and kernel hot-path spikes, increasing P95/P99 latency and evictions. Existing tickets push on compaction, eviction heuristics, and kernel steering, but there is no lightweight coordinator that reasons jointly about KV granularity and decode-wave alignment at runtime.
proposed_solution: Introduce a Paged KV Granularity Harmonizer component in the serving runtime with two responsibilities: (A) Granularity policy: during prefill decide whether to allocate fragments as independent pages or coalesce them into a temporary micro-view based on recent touch frequency, estimated reuse, and current residency pressure; (B) Decode-wave fairness: introduce a small scheduler that assigns decode wave offsets (0..N-1) per request/tenant subject to latency SLO buckets so that prefill+decode work is spread over micro-windows, lowering concurrent kernel demand. The harmonizer exposes knobs: coalescing threshold (bytes / token-span), max micro-view residency time, and fairness window size. It integrates with existing KV allocator and kernel selector via a lightweight advisory API (no blocking changes to kernel paths).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (experiment): 1) Add harmonizer module with in-memory policy and feature flag; 2) Implement micro-view allocation path which creates temporary contiguous KV mappings for short-lived fragments; 3) Implement decode-wave offset tagging in request metadata and soft scheduler that delays decode start by slot*slot_duration when safe; 4) Telemetry: track per-request decode offset, fragment coalescing events, eviction counts, and kernel hot-path contention metrics. Phase 2 (tuning): 5) Run A/B on low-traffic cluster with synthetic small/large mixed workload; 6) Tune thresholds and slot duration; 7) Expose admin knobs in console for Dedicated/Private. Phase 3 (rollout): 8) Gradual rollout with canary, monitor regressions, full release in runtime-1.22.
milestones: M1: Harmonizer module stub + feature flag (2026-02-25)
M2: Micro-view allocation + decode offset tagging (2026-03-04)
M3: Telemetry dashboards and A/B harness (2026-03-11)
acceptance_criteria: P95 decode latency for mixed small/large workload reduced by >= 15% on canary hosts compared to baseline
Eviction rate (evictions/sec) decreased by >= 20% for workloads with >50% short traces
No regression in median token throughput for large-batch workloads (<5% drop)
Harmonizer feature flag can be toggled at runtime with safe rollback and no allocator crashes
Telemetry surfaces coalescing events, decode offsets, and per-kernel contention; dashboards documented
test_plan: Unit tests for micro-view allocation and release paths
Integration test: run mixed traffic replay (live traces) against a canary cluster with and without harmonizer to capture latency and eviction deltas
Fault injection: simulate delayed decode starts and ensure requests meet SLOs or fall back to immediate decode path
Load test: confirm kernel selector behavior unchanged for homogeneous large-batch workloads
Correctness: ensure KV lookup semantics are equivalent (micro-view is a read-only coalesced mapping with same content as separate fragments)
risks: Micro-view coalescing could increase peak memory usage if thresholds are too permissive
Decode-wave staggering might increase median latency for latency-sensitive single-request workflows if slot durations are misconfigured
Interaction with existing eviction heuristics could create oscillations (coalesce -> retain -> eviction -> repeat)
Instrumentation overhead could slightly increase CPU/GC on control-plane threads if telemetry is too verbose
